title.narrative: Strengthen Media Institutions in Climate Action and Disaster Management

description.narrative:
Media institutions, whether broadcast, print or digital, perform an integral function throughout a disaster management cycle. Yet, they can be vulnerable to the very disruptions they are relied upon to report, and can fulfil this mission effectively only when they have the right strategies, capacities, and tools at their disposal. Strengthening media institutions and their personnel to be more prepared and resilient is therefore essential, not only for their own continuity, but for the communities that depend on them for accessing reliable information and voicing their needs, particularly in times of crisis.
Through a multifaceted approach, the programme described in this work plan will provide strategic guidance and technical support to media institutions to reinforce their capacities and practices for reporting on climate change and natural hazards and for disaster preparedness and response. As societal actors, media institutions will have stronger editorial capacities and technological capabilities to address these topics as a core part of their public interest mandate. As organizations, they will also establish robust internal policies and frameworks to prepare for and respond to disasters.
As a result, Member States will be supported in their efforts for climate change adaptation and mitigation and disaster preparedness and response. With enhanced access to reliable media content throughout the disaster management cycle, from prevention and preparedness to response and recovery, people, particularly the most vulnerable, will be better equipped to make informed decisions and build greater resilience in the face of the increasing extreme weather events and disasters.
